title: How to Make a Horror Movie With AI in 6 Steps
summary: How to make a horror movie with AI in 6 steps, from the fear to the final cut, with the real prompts behind Xenogenesis, a sci-fi horror film made in Flick.
body_markdown:
### What are the key elements of a horror movie?


A fear the audience recognises, a character who cannot escape it, and dread built through light, sound and what the camera holds back before any scare arrives. Most horror films also give the threat a signature, a sound, a colour or a trait, so it can be felt before it is seen.


### How do you make a horror movie scary without gore?


Keep the threat off screen and let sound carry it: a scream behind a door, a breath close to the microphone, a silence where music would be. A slow camera that holds on an empty doorway or staircase makes the viewer search the frame, which is often scarier than anything you could show.


### What camera shots are used in horror movies?


Handheld close-ups for panic, a Dutch angle (the frame tilted off its axis) for unease, a dolly zoom or vertigo move for shock, point-of-view shots from the threat, and long holds on empty space. Use one at a time, and save the strongest for the scare itself.


### How long should a horror short film be?


A first horror short can be one to five minutes, long enough for one fear and one scare. Most festival shorts run under 15 minutes, and the Academy counts a film as a short at 40 minutes or less, credits included.


### What are good horror short film ideas?


Ideas that turn something ordinary against the hero: a body that changes, a home that is not empty, a loved one who is slightly wrong, a warning nobody believes. Pick one fear, one location and one or two characters, so the whole idea fits in a few scenes.


### Can AI make a horror movie?


Yes. AI video models make the shots, image models make the characters and settings, and the prompts can carry the camera, the light and the sound of each scene. The fear, the pacing and the choice of what to hide still come from the filmmaker writing those prompts.

You can start for free. Flick gives you 100 credits when you sign up and 200 more for joining the Flick Discord; Seedance 2.0, the video model behind most Xenogenesis clips, needs the Standard plan.
